Officials said US aircraft carrier and destroyer avoided attacks before three Iranian tankers were struck by the US The US military said Saturday it struck three Iranian oil tankers after US navy warships came under missile attack, further escalating tensions in the region and warning it would “if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet”. According to the military, a US aircraft carrier and destroyer avoided “multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks” while patrolling the region. No US personnel were injured. Two of the Iranian oil carriers were “permanently disabled”, the Pentagon said, while a third tanker, which was unladen, was destroyed. The US said the vessels were part of a shadow network that helped finance Iran’s powerful Revolutionary Guards and armed proxy groups operating across the region.

U.S. forces struck three Iranian crude oil tankers in the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman Saturday morning as part of a new "tanker for tanker" retaliatory policy meant to further deter Iranian attacks on tankers that move through the Strait of Hormuz shipping lane. An oil products tanker is anchored in the Strait of Hormuz on Aug. 10, 2026. U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) said American forces "permanently disabled" the three oil carriers near Iran's Kharg Island, Jask port city and in the Gulf of Oman. The attacks come after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched ballistic missiles toward two U.S. Navy warships.

“We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet,” the head of US Central Command, Adm Brad Cooper, said in the statement. The announcement followed an earlier report from Iran that the US had attacked an Iranian tanker near Kharg Island in the Gulf. Tasnim, a semiofficial news outlet affiliated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, reported the strike happened on Saturday morning. It said the tanker’s crew survived and was being evacuated. The US said one tanker was struck off Kharg Island, while another was hit near Jask. The unladen tanker was struck in the Gulf of Oman. The US statement also shared what it described as video footage of the strikes.

[Lähde: The Guardian World | URL: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/05/us-military-iran-tankers]
Officials said US aircraft carrier and destroyer avoided attacks before three Iranian tankers were struck by the US

The US military said Saturday it struck three Iranian oil tankers after US navy warships came under missile attack, further escalating tensions in the region and warning it would “if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet”.

According to the military, a US aircraft carrier and destroyer avoided “multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks” while patrolling the region. No US personnel were injured.

Two of the Iranian oil carriers were “permanently disabled”, the Pentagon said, while a third tanker, which was unladen, was destroyed.

The US said the vessels were part of a shadow network that helped finance Iran’s powerful Revolutionary Guards and armed proxy groups operating across the region.

“We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet,” the head of US Central Command, Adm Brad Cooper, said in the statement.

The announcement followed an earlier report from Iran that the US had attacked an Iranian tanker near Kharg Island in the Gulf. Tasnim, a semiofficial news outlet affiliated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, reported the strike happened on Saturday morning. It said the tanker’s crew survived and was being evacuated.

The US said one tanker was struck off Kharg Island, while another was hit near Jask. The unladen tanker was struck in the Gulf of Oman. The US statement also shared what it described as video footage of the strikes.

The latest attacks came nearly a week after the US and Iran resumed strikes after about a month of relative calm in the on-again, off-again war that began with US and Israeli attacks in February. Attempts at negotiations have collapsed.

One of the strikes hit a wedding in southern Iran on Tuesday, killing four people, including a child, and injuring dozens, according to Iranian officials.

The US vice-president, JD Vance, said “sometimes things happen” when asked on Thursday whether an US strike was responsible for killing people at the wedding celebration.

The renewed strikes have also brought fresh scrutiny to a 28 February US attack in Minab that struck a school compound and killed at least 156 people, most of them schoolchildren.

A preliminary US military inquiry reportedly found that the attack resulted from a targeting error after outdated coordinates identified the school as part of a nearby Revolutionary Guard

The attacks come after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched ballistic missiles toward two U.S. Navy warships.

The U.S. ships were able to avoid the missiles and no injuries or deaths were reported, but Saturday's retaliatory attacks are among the first under a new policy that will target Iranian tankers in response to every Iranian attack on a ship in the Strait of Hormuz.

The "tanker for tanker" policy is meant to stop Iran from attacking ships trying to use the vital oil shipping channel and aims to dismantle the military infrastructure—like radar, air defense and missile capabilities—that Iran uses to threaten maritime traffic.

The tanker strikes came after CENTCOM conducted raids against approximately 100 military targets earlier this week, focusing on Iranian air defenses, coastal radar sites, mine-laying ships and anti-ship cruise missile launch pads along the Strait of Hormuz.

vNo injuries have yet been reported from Saturday's attacks, and multiple news outlets reported Americans warned the ships via radio ahead of the strikes, giving crew time to evacuate.

"Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost—taking out three of yours," Adm. Brad Cooper, CENTCOM commander, said Saturday. "We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran's limited and exposed oil fleet."

Negotiators have failed to secure a peace framework since U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran launched the region into war earlier this year.
